newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wattyl sees higher 97/98 Australia profit.
newsitem.headline: Wattyl sees higher 97/98 Australia profit.

text.p: Paint manufacturer Wattyl Ltd said on Wednesday it expected higher sales and profit from its Australian operations, which make up the bulk of the group activies, in the year to June 30, 1998.

"Initiatives instituted during the (1996/97) year, together with planned new product launches should contribute to a further improvement in sales and profits in the 1997/98 year," Wattyl said in a statement accompanying its 1996/97 results.
Wattyl earlier reported a net profit of A$25.81 million in the year to June 30, 1997, compared with A$20.31 million ayear earlier.
Wattyl said the Australian paint market remained subdued throughout the 1996/97 year and strong competition maintained pressure on profit margins.

Turning to Asia, Wattyl said Indonesia, Thailand and Malaysia had strong sales and profit growth, building on the gains achieved in the previous year. Singapore underperformed during the year and partly eroded gains made by the other units.
"Restructuring in Singapore is expected to reverse this situation in the coming year," Wattyl said.
It said its New Zealand business had an improved year, helped by the Taubman acquisition.

Wattyl said the United States operations substantially improved sales and profits during 1996/97. The Coronado, Premier and Lenmar businesses, in the later part of the year, contributed strongly to U.S. profitability, it said.

"Restructuring of the original Georgia, North Carolina and Florida businesses resulted in a significant improvement of their operating results and further gains are expected to be made this year," Wattyl said.
"The paint market in the U.S.A. has had strong growth in 1996/97 and this is expected to continue through 1997/98," it said.
Wattyl shares closed one cent lower at A$6.74 on Wednesday.
